interpretation: Phylogenetic-memory architecture is at least two-dimensional. L quantifies repeatable lineage-wide memory level, whereas A quantifies stability of how memory is allocated among traits. In both compilations A is low and model-predicted pair-order reversal closely matches direct observed reversal. Memory level and allocation disagreement are nearly uncorrelated across families.
conceptual_claim: A lineage can have a repeatable overall level of phylogenetic memory without inheriting a stable allocation of that memory among traits.
hard_nonclaims: AusTraits residual variance is not measurement-error-separated and should not be called a pure biological family-by-trait interaction.
L and A are model-based architecture indices, not evolutionary rates.
Null level-allocation correlation does not prove exact independence.

signal_to_contingency_portability_law.predictor: x = absolute leave-one-family-out trait-mean contrast / sqrt(2 * sigma2_system)
signal_to_contingency_portability_law.interpretation: On S3, pairwise trait-order portability is calibrated by a common signal-to-contingency ratio across BIEN and AusTraits. The global trait contrast behaves as a probabilistic prior whose predictive strength is set by its magnitude relative to lineage-specific trait deviation. The fitted slope is below the idealized Gaussian-theory value of 1, so the simple Gaussian equation is directionally useful but overconfident.
signal_to_contingency_portability_law.prune_sensitivity: Positive calibration is less clean on prune-only; source and slope interactions are not statistically resolved, but the common BIEN slope is weak. Treat the cross-compilation law as S3-primary with prune sensitivity rather than fully tree-axis invariant.
